variants.title: Follow the lifecycle
variants.context: An LLM’s lifecycle: define and curate data, pretrain a base model, adapt behavior, serve token generation, then evaluate and operate with a tested rollback.
variants.prompt: A model goes from data to production. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Evaluate and operate: gate versions on evidence, monitor drift, keep a rollback.
Serve token generation: prefill and decode, quotas, tools, output validation.
Define and curate data: lawful sources, deduplication, mixtures, provenance, holdouts.
Pretrain a base model while tracking loss, contamination, and checkpoint health.
Adapt behavior with prompts, retrieval, supervised examples, or preference data.

variants.hint: Adaptation sits between pretraining and serving.
variants.explanation: Data → pretrain → adapt → serve → evaluate and operate. A failure at any stage appears later as a wrong answer or an unmanageable rollback.

variants.title: Follow the lifecycle
variants.context: An LLM’s lifecycle: define and curate data, pretrain a base model, adapt behavior, serve token generation, then evaluate and operate with a tested rollback.
variants.prompt: A wrong answer is traced back. Put the stages that could have caused it in order.

items.text: Evaluation had no slice for this failure.
Serving assembled stale context.
Pretraining optimized token prediction, not factuality.
Adaptation did not cover the task.
Data curation admitted duplicated or contaminated material.

variants.hint: Each stage has its own failure mode.
variants.explanation: Falling pretraining loss does not prove product reliability.

variants.title: Follow the lifecycle
variants.context: An LLM’s lifecycle: define and curate data, pretrain a base model, adapt behavior, serve token generation, then evaluate and operate with a tested rollback.
variants.prompt: A new checkpoint is being released. Put the release loop in order.

items.text: Gate on task, safety, latency, and cost evidence with a tested rollback.
Confirm the base checkpoint and its evaluation.
Re-run adaptation against the new base if adapters are involved.
Confirm the data snapshot and lineage.
Deploy the pinned bundle to serving.

variants.hint: An adapter may not stay compatible with a different base.
variants.explanation: Roll back the complete model bundle.

variants.title: Pick the layer
variants.context: Adapt only the layer that needs to change: prompts and examples for temporary instructions and output shape; retrieval for volatile or private evidence; supervised adaptation for a stable pattern defined by examples; preference optimization for broad behavior.
variants.prompt: The output must switch to a new JSON shape for one feature, and it may change next week. Which layer?
options: Prompt and examples.
Supervised fine-tuning.
Preference optimization.
optionFeedback: Temporary instructions and output shape belong in request state.
Fine-tuning makes the change more persistent than necessary.
Preference data shapes broad behavior, not one format.
variants.hint: How persistent should this change be?
variants.explanation: Use the least persistent mechanism that works.

variants.title: Pick the layer
variants.context: Adapt only the layer that needs to change: prompts and examples for temporary instructions and output shape; retrieval for volatile or private evidence; supervised adaptation for a stable pattern defined by examples; preference optimization for broad behavior.
variants.prompt: Answers must cite this week’s private policy documents, which change often and must be deletable. Which layer?
options: Retrieval grounding with source identity and freshness.
Fine-tuning weekly on the current policy documents.
A longer system prompt that carries the policy text inline.
optionFeedback: Volatile, private evidence needs independent deletion and provenance.
Weights cannot be un-trained per document, so a deleted policy still shapes answers.
Prompts do not scale to the whole corpus and cannot authorize per reader.
variants.hint: Can the knowledge be deleted independently later?
variants.explanation: Retrieval keeps external knowledge outside the weights.

variants.title: Pick the layer
variants.context: Adapt only the layer that needs to change: prompts and examples for temporary instructions and output shape; retrieval for volatile or private evidence; supervised adaptation for a stable pattern defined by examples; preference optimization for broad behavior.
variants.prompt: A stable classification pattern is defined by thousands of representative examples, and prompting has stalled. Which layer?
options: Preference optimization over ranked pairs of answers.
Supervised adaptation, measured against the prompt baseline.
A bigger prompt holding a few hundred of the examples.
optionFeedback: Preference data is for broad ranked behavior, not one example-defined label set.
A learned pattern is justified when lighter mechanisms remain insufficient.
Prompt scaling has already stalled, and thousands of examples do not fit the window.
variants.hint: Is the behavior stable and example-defined?
variants.explanation: Match adaptation evidence to its persistence.

variants.title: Read the serving numbers
variants.context: Prefill processes the prompt in parallel; decode emits tokens one at a time. Time to first token and time per output token describe different experiences. A larger batch improves throughput but can hurt first-token latency. Prefix reuse is safe only when the cached prefix identity includes every input that changes its result.
variants.prompt: Users complain the assistant “thinks” too long before text appears, though total time is fine. Which metric is the problem?
options: Time per output token.
Total tokens.
Time to first token.
optionFeedback: Per-token cadence is fine here.
Count is not the complaint.
Prefill and queueing delay the first token.
variants.hint: Which experience is the user describing?
variants.explanation: Report time to first token and time per output token separately, with tails.

variants.title: Read the serving numbers
variants.context: Prefill processes the prompt in parallel; decode emits tokens one at a time. Time to first token and time per output token describe different experiences. A larger batch improves throughput but can hurt first-token latency. Prefix reuse is safe only when the cached prefix identity includes every input that changes its result.
variants.prompt: Increasing batch size raised throughput but first-token latency got worse. Why?
options: The tokenizer slowed down under the larger input volume.
Larger batches wait longer to fill and share prefill compute.
Batching is free, so the measurement must be noise.
optionFeedback: Tokenization is a small fixed cost per request and does not grow with batch size.
Scheduling trades queue delay against batching efficiency.
There is a real trade-off: throughput rises while each request waits longer to start.
variants.hint: What does a request wait for in a larger batch?
variants.explanation: Scheduling trades queue delay against batching efficiency.

variants.title: Read the serving numbers
variants.context: Prefill processes the prompt in parallel; decode emits tokens one at a time. Time to first token and time per output token describe different experiences. A larger batch improves throughput but can hurt first-token latency. Prefix reuse is safe only when the cached prefix identity includes every input that changes its result.
variants.prompt: A prefix cache is keyed on the system prompt only, but the tool schema changed. What happens?
options: Nothing; the tool schema is sent separately from the prefix.
The cache invalidates itself once the schema version changes.
Cached prefill is reused for a different effective input.
optionFeedback: Tool schemas sit in the prefix and change the prefill result, whatever the API calls them.
Nothing invalidates a cache keyed on the wrong thing, because the key never saw the schema.
Prefix reuse is safe only when the cached identity covers every input that changes the result.
variants.hint: What inputs change the prefill result?
variants.explanation: Prefix reuse can skip work only when the cached identity is complete.

variants.title: Think in bundles
variants.context: Product behavior comes from the complete model bundle and request path, not a model name. Two checkpoints in one family can differ in context contract, tool behavior, memory, license, and failure profile. Roll back the complete bundle.
variants.prompt: Two checkpoints share a family name. May you swap one for the other without evidence?
options: Yes; checkpoints in one family share a context contract.
Yes, if the smaller one is cheaper at the same benchmark score.
No. Context contract, tool behavior, license, and failure profile vary.
optionFeedback: A shared name is a naming boundary, not a guarantee about window, tools, or memory.
Cost does not establish equivalence, and a benchmark score hides the failure profile you ship against.
Compare the exact bundle you deploy.
variants.explanation: Behavior comes from the complete bundle and request path.

variants.title: Think in bundles
variants.context: Product behavior comes from the complete model bundle and request path, not a model name. Two checkpoints in one family can differ in context contract, tool behavior, memory, license, and failure profile. Roll back the complete bundle.
variants.prompt: A rollback restores the old adapter but keeps the new base checkpoint. What is the risk?
options: The adapter may not be compatible with a different base or runtime.
No risk; the adapter carries all of the behavior that regressed.
Inference gets faster because the new base is better optimized.
optionFeedback: Adapter and base are one contract, evaluated together.
A partial rollback creates a base and adapter combination that was never evaluated.
Speed is not the concern; the combination has no evaluation evidence behind it.
variants.explanation: Track base, tokenizer, adapter, code, data, and evaluator versions together.

variants.title: Think in bundles
variants.context: Product behavior comes from the complete model bundle and request path, not a model name. Two checkpoints in one family can differ in context contract, tool behavior, memory, license, and failure profile. Roll back the complete bundle.
variants.prompt: Pretraining loss fell. Does the product get more reliable?
options: Not necessarily; factuality and tool correctness need their own evidence.
Yes; lower loss means the model predicts the right answer more often.
Yes, in proportion to how far the loss fell across the run.
optionFeedback: The objective rewards token prediction, not the behaviors the product depends on.
Lower loss means better token prediction on the training distribution, not being right.
There is no proportional law linking a loss curve to instruction following or safety.
variants.hint: What does the training objective reward?
variants.explanation: Do not infer product reliability from falling pretraining loss.

variants.title: Run one training step
variants.context: One autoregressive training step: tokenize the sequence, mix the visible prefix through attention and feed-forward layers, project the final representation to a distribution over the vocabulary, compare it with the target token, and update the parameters.
variants.prompt: One autoregressive training step runs. Put it in order.

items.text: Project the final representation into a probability distribution over the vocabulary.
Convert source content into token IDs and positions under a versioned tokenizer.
Compare with the target token and update parameters to reduce future error.
Attention and feed-forward layers mix the visible prefix into contextual representations.

variants.hint: The target supervises a distribution; it is not copied into a table.
variants.explanation: Pretraining learns a distribution, not a fact database.

variants.title: Run one training step
variants.context: One autoregressive training step: tokenize the sequence, mix the visible prefix through attention and feed-forward layers, project the final representation to a distribution over the vocabulary, compare it with the target token, and update the parameters.
variants.prompt: Duplicated data enters training. Put the step in order and note where duplication distorts it.

items.text: Produce the distribution.
Tokenize the sequence, including the duplicated text.
Mix the prefix.
Compare with the target; repeated examples over-weight those patterns in the update.

variants.hint: Every repeated example is another gradient step in its favor.
variants.explanation: Measure duplication and contamination before training.

variants.title: Run one training step
variants.context: One autoregressive training step: tokenize the sequence, mix the visible prefix through attention and feed-forward layers, project the final representation to a distribution over the vocabulary, compare it with the target token, and update the parameters.
variants.prompt: A held-out slice is evaluated. Put the forward pass in order, ending without an update.

items.text: Project to the vocabulary distribution.
Compare with the target to measure loss; no parameter update on held-out data.
Tokenize the held-out text.
Mix the visible prefix.

variants.hint: Evaluation uses the same forward pass without the update.
variants.explanation: Preserve held-out slices that represent real tasks and difficult failures.
